name: design-canvas
description: A live, EDITABLE Claude Design canvas in a pane - the real pan/zoom canvas editor from Claude Code's bundled `design` skill, seeded from `.dc.html` artboard files in a folder on disk, re-seeded automatically whenever one of them changes, and able to write the user's own edits back into those same files. Reach for it whenever the work is VISUAL and you are drafting it as files: a UI mockup or screen flow, a landing page, a poster/flyer/one-pager, a report laid out as artboards. Mount it once and the user WATCHES the layout change as you write it instead of reading you describe it, pins comments on the artboards, and can click straight into the design and change it. It is not a viewer for someone else's work: it only ever shows canvases seeded from the user's OWN local working files, never an Artifact URL and never a published canvas - which is also what makes writing back to them the right behaviour rather than a liberty. EDIT MODE, and SAVE IS REAL: the pane installs the editor's one-member host object before the canvas boots, so the user gets the actual editing chrome - click-to-select with a quick menu (font family, size, colour, Properties), inline rich-text editing, undo/redo, zoom, and a working Save. Save hands the complete edited document to the pane, which posts it to a loopback listener the SERVICE owns (127.0.0.1, ephemeral port, POST only, per-spawn path token, published as `dsn_canvas.save_endpoint` - never through the store, so a 2.5 MB document never enters the event ring or a committed graph node, and only the page's state block, under 1% of it, makes the hop), and the service runs the seeding helper's own `--extract` to turn it back into files. The write discipline is the point: nothing under the folder is touched until that extract exits clean AND returns at least one artboard; every file about to be replaced is copied into the service's own build tree first; each file is write-then-rename; a failure part-way rolls the whole batch back; it NEVER deletes, so an artboard removed inside the editor is reported as orphaned and its file left alone; and `canvas.json` is compared by MEANING rather than bytes, so a save that changed no layout leaves a hand-formatted manifest byte-identical. The watcher then ignores exactly those writes and the service re-seeds ONCE, deliberately, instead of fighting the editor. THE CONSEQUENCE FOR YOU: these files have a second author. Re-read before assuming what is on disk, and never blind-overwrite a file the user may just have edited on the canvas - `Read` then `Edit`, never a whole-file `Write` from your own earlier draft, which silently discards their work. No save wakes you and no save writes a store key you get pushed; you notice from `dsn_files[].mtime`, a bumped `dsn_canvas.seq`, or because the user says so. SERVICE-BACKED, so it is inert until the user runs `claude-web-chat trust design-canvas` in their TERMINAL: say that command in chat in the same breath as mounting the pane, because the pane can only name it and cannot grant it - and describe it accurately, because it is a WRITE grant now. The service reads the artboards under `dir`, runs the seeding helper, and writes back into `dir` when the user hits Save and ONLY then; seeding, watching, the derived `canvas.json`, the backups and every diagnostic go to its own build directory under `.web-chat/`. Consent is keyed on (project root, service.js contents, params), so changing `dir`, `title`, `isolate`, `watch` or any of the frame params (`frame_w`, `frame_h`, `expand`, `wide_scan`) asks again - `routing` does not, being shell-read - and the service runs only while its pane is on the ACTIVE node with a browser watching (navigate away and it stops, navigate back and it respawns). Editing therefore depends on the SESSION, not on the file: untrusted, stopped, or off the active node, the canvas still edits on screen but Save has nowhere to land and fails the recoverable way ("your changes are kept - try again") with nothing reaching disk. `isolate: true` turns editing off outright along with pins - an opaque-origin frame can neither be read from nor be handed a host object - which is the right trade only for content the user did not author. It also needs Claude Design to exist on this machine: the editor payload is materialised into a temp directory the first time the bundled `design` skill runs in a session, so if it never has, the pane renders state `no-payload` and the one fix is to run `/design` once in Claude Code. FRAME SIZES: an artboard is drawn inside a fixed w x h frame that comes from `canvas.json`, and with no `canvas.json` the editor frames EVERY artboard at its own 800x600 default - silently, since the helper only reports w/h values that are present and non-numeric, never missing ones - so a 1288-wide design is drawn small and clipped, which reads as a broken pane. So the service derives a frame per artboard from the source (a `$preview` in data-props, then a fixed px box on the root element, then the `frame_w`/`frame_h` params, then a 1440-wide default) and writes the manifest into its own build directory, NEVER into `dir`: the whole `canvas.json` when there is none, and otherwise only the keys the user's own manifest LEFT OUT. An explicit `canvas.json` always wins - a value they wrote is passed through untouched, wrong values included, and a manifest that does not parse or would be refused is handed to the helper as written so its fatal stderr names THEIR file. SCROLLING: `$preview` is also the thing that makes an artboard scrollable. An artboard that declares none gets `html,body{height:100%;margin:0}` injected by support.js, which pins the document to its frame so it cannot scroll at all and the wheel chains out to the surface page - so any design taller than its frame needs a `$preview` in its data-props, or its own `overflow:auto` container, or the rest of it is simply unreachable. Writes `dsn_canvas` - `{seq, ok, state, payload_component, title, artboards, layout, frames, warnings, seeded_at, bytes, upstream, save_endpoint, error, hint}`, where `state` is one of ready | seeding | no-payload | bad-dir | seed-failed | live-store, and every failure carries human prose in `error` plus the ONE action that fixes it in `hint` (a `seed-failed` carries the seeding helper's stderr verbatim, which is written to be read). `layout` says where the layout came from - user | user-filled | synthesised | none | null - and `frames` is `[{file, w, h, source, expand}]` whose `source` names the rung the size came from - canvas.json | $preview | root-style | param | wide-scan | default, or null when nothing framed that artboard and the editor's 800x600 applies - so a frame that is a guess can be seen to be one. `save_endpoint` belongs to the PANE: never post to it yourself and never repeat its token, but missing or empty while `state` is `ready` means editing works on screen and a Save cannot land. Also writes `dsn_files` `{seq, dir, files:[{name, bytes, mtime}], has_canvas_json}`, which is the cheapest way to see what is actually on disk - including whether a save changed something - without a second read. Reads the CONTROL key `dsn_ctl {seq, op}` - `op` `reseed` (re-run the helper against the current files, always safe) or `rescan` (re-read the directory listing only) - which the service watches over SSE: a user panning, zooming, clicking, editing or SAVING never wakes Claude. You may drive it yourself, but `set_store` needs its patch wrapper - `set_store({patch:{dsn_ctl:{seq:Date.now(), op:'reseed'}}})` - a bare `set_store({dsn_ctl:...})` is a silent no-op that still returns ok, and `seq` must strictly increase or the write is ignored. ONE declared signal, `dsn_ask {seq, note, artboard}`, written only when the user hits Ask Claude: declare it TOP-LEVEL on use_component (`signals:[{key:'dsn_ask', wake:'queue'}]`) while `routing:'none'` goes INSIDE `params`. That asymmetry is the easiest thing here to get wrong - use_component reads `signals` only at the top level and `routing` only inside params, and each is dropped in silence in the wrong place. `routing:'none'` does not suppress the signal; the queue classifier tests declared keys before the routing opt-out. Params: `dir` and `title` are required, `title` being CONTENT-named because the seeding helper hard-refuses a title that names the tool instead of the design; `isolate:true` sandboxes the frame and turns pins AND editing off; `watch:false` stops the 250 ms-debounced re-seed but does not stop saving; and `frame_w`, `frame_h`, `expand` and `wide_scan` size the frames the service has to DERIVE, none of which can override a value the user wrote in their own `canvas.json`. There is no `edit` switch - a mounted canvas is editable whenever the service is running and `isolate` is off, which is the intended default. Two degraded contexts it handles rather than blanking: node previews and glance cards get a static placeholder (their CSP is `default-src 'none'`, so both the frame and the fetch are dead) and so do frozen exports (the pane's fetch runs against no server, and an exported canvas cannot save) - the right export for a canvas is the seeded `.html` itself, which is already self-contained and interactive. It also needs a SECURE CONTEXT: fine on localhost, 127.0.0.1 and https, but over plain http to a LAN IP or an mDNS name the canvas hangs on a permanent spinner, so the pane warns before mounting the frame. Finally, the service writes a runtime-only carrier component into this project to hand the 2.4 MB editor to the pane. Its name is `design-canvas-payload-<8 hex>` - per MOUNT, not fixed, so two design-canvas panes on one node cannot clobber each other's payload; never hardcode it, read `dsn_canvas.payload_component` for the real one. It shows up in list_components, the drawer and the command palette. NEVER mount it: one accidental mount snapshots 2.4 MB into every committed graph node, forever.

dir.title: Folder holding the artboard files - an absolute path, and the canvas can write back into it
dir.description: ABSOLUTE path to the working directory whose `.dc.html` artboards make up this canvas. It must already contain at least one `<Name>.dc.html`; a missing, unreadable or artboard-less folder renders state `bad-dir` naming the path and what was expected, never a silent fallback. THIS IS A TWO-WAY DOOR: the service reads these files to seed the canvas, and when the user hits Save in the editor it writes their edits back into them - the only code path in the whole service that touches anything here, and it is guarded (extract first, back up every replaced file into the service's own build tree, write-then-rename per file, roll the batch back on failure, never delete). So point it at a folder that holds THIS DESIGN and nothing else, not at a folder that also holds source you would mind the canvas rewriting; the project root is refused outright, because it would contain the service's own build directory. `canvas.json` beside the artboards is optional and supplies the layout (per-artboard x/y/w/h, sticky notes, pages, launch); when it is there it is authoritative - the service only fills in keys it leaves out, and never rewrites one it sets - and when it is not, the service derives the whole manifest into its own build directory so the artboards are framed at their real size rather than the editor's 800x600 default. A layout the user changes ON the canvas does come back through Save, so `canvas.json` is itself a file that can change under you; formatting alone does not, because it is compared by meaning. See `frame_w`/`frame_h`/`expand`/`wide_scan`, and read `dsn_canvas.layout` and `dsn_canvas.frames[].source` to see where each frame came from. Images (.png .jpg .jpeg .gif .webp .avif .bmp .svg) in the folder are picked up automatically and stored inside the canvas, so keep each one small - the editor drops any file entry over 2 MiB at load. The path is FENCED inside the project: one that resolves outside it is refused as `bad-dir` rather than read. Changing this re-asks the `claude-web-chat trust design-canvas` approval, which is correct, because it names the files this service may read AND rewrite.

title.title: What this design is called - name it from the content, not from the tool
title.description: The canvas's own title. It lands in the page title and in the seeded state block, and a slug of it names the seeded file. The seeding helper enforces this and exits 1 on a bad value, which surfaces as state `seed-failed` with its stderr verbatim, so get it right at spawn time: it is REFUSED if it is empty, over 120 characters, contains a less-than, greater-than, ampersand, double-quote, backslash or control character (apostrophes are fine), or is one of the generic names that describe the tool rather than the design - design, canvas, design canvas, new design, untitled, appifact, new appifact, artifact - compared case-insensitively after trimming. Name it the way the user would refer to it.

isolate.title: Sandbox the canvas frame - safer, but turns editing, Save and pins off completely
isolate.description: Leave this off for the normal case, which is the only case this component supports: artboards you or the user authored in `dir`. Turning it on sandboxes the canvas frame to an opaque origin, so nothing inside it can reach the local daemon - the right stance for any content you would not vouch for. The cost is total, and it is now two things rather than one. An opaque-origin frame cannot be read from, so no anchors can be projected and pins are unavailable; and it cannot be handed the editor's host object, so the canvas boots READ-ONLY - pan, zoom, look, and anything nudged on screen is gone on the next reload. Use it only when the trade is the point: showing a canvas that is not the user's own. Changing this re-asks the `claude-web-chat trust design-canvas` approval.

watch.title: Re-seed automatically when a file in the folder changes
watch.description: On by default, and it is what makes the pane worth mounting: the service watches `dir` for changes to `*.dc.html`, `canvas.json` and images, debounces them for 250 ms, re-runs the seeding helper and bumps `dsn_canvas.seq` - so the canvas keeps up with the files you write, with no turn of yours involved. It does not fight the editor: a Save writes to `dir` too, so the service suppresses the watcher for exactly the paths it just wrote and then re-seeds ONCE, deliberately, rather than looping. Turn it off for a frozen snapshot, or when a build process rewrites the folder in a way that would thrash the re-seed - saving still works either way, and the post-save re-seed still runs. You can force one at any time by writing the control key: `set_store({patch:{dsn_ctl:{seq:Date.now(), op:'reseed'}}})`. Changing this re-asks the `claude-web-chat trust design-canvas` approval.

frame_w.title: Frame width in px - only for artboards that do not declare their own size
frame_w.description: How wide to frame an artboard whose source says nothing about its size. Leave it empty unless a design comes out framed wrong. Order of precedence: an artboard's own `$preview` width in its data-props wins, then a fixed px width on its root element, then this, then a 1440 px default - a per-artboard declaration in the file beats a setting that applies to the whole canvas. Values are clamped to 120-8000, the range the editor itself accepts. It can never override a width set in the folder's own `canvas.json`; it only fills a gap that file leaves. Check `dsn_canvas.frames[].source` afterwards to see which rung each artboard actually landed on.

frame_h.title: Frame height in px - same rule as the width
frame_h.description: How tall to frame an artboard whose source says nothing about its height. Same precedence and the same 120-8000 clamp as the width, and equally unable to override a height the folder's own `canvas.json` sets. When nothing supplies a height, one is derived from the width (three quarters of it, and never under 1024) - deliberately generous, because a frame that is too tall only costs blank canvas while one that is too short CUTS THE DESIGN OFF: an artboard that declares no `$preview` has `html,body{height:100%;margin:0}` injected into it, which pins the document to its frame so it cannot scroll at all. A design taller than its frame needs a `$preview` in its data-props, or its own `overflow:auto` container - this param cannot substitute for one.

expand.title: Fit or fill - how a focused artboard uses the window
expand.description: `auto` (the default) decides per artboard from the same evidence that decided its size: a design that declares an intrinsic size gets `fit`, and one that is fluid AND can scroll gets `fill`. `fit` keeps the artboard at its own size and scales the view DOWN to fit the window, never up. `fill` resizes the frame to the window and draws it at scale 1, which is right only for a fluid-width root that can scroll - a `height:100%` design with no internal scroll container is CLIPPED in fill, permanently, while in fit it merely shrinks. Setting `fit` or `fill` here forces that value on EVERY artboard; `auto` is almost always the better answer, and the editor's own Fit/Fill toggle still flips it live either way. Note that this only affects a FOCUSED artboard: zoomed out on the canvas every artboard is drawn at its own w x h, so this cannot rescue a wrong frame size - only the width and height can. It never overrides an `expand` set in the folder's own `canvas.json`.

wide_scan.title: Guess an artboard's width from the widest box declared anywhere in it
wide_scan.description: A last-resort fallback for a design that declares no `$preview` and has no fixed-width root, but does contain one wide shell somewhere - a `max-width: 1288px` article, say. With this on, the widest px width found in the source (between 320 and 8000) is used as the frame width when nothing better exists. Off by default because it is a heuristic reading of markup rather than a declaration, and a wrong guess frames the design wrong. Any frame that rests on it reads `wide-scan` in `dsn_canvas.frames[].source`, so a guess can always be told apart from a declaration. Prefer declaring a `$preview` in the artboard - which also makes it scrollable - or writing a `canvas.json` with real sizes; a width set there always wins over this.

routing.title: Activity routing - leave this as none
routing.description: `none` is the only valid value. Without it every pan, zoom, selection and inline edit on the canvas coalesces into per-mount activity items that reach the queue on the user's next Push - pure noise, because this pane has a deliberate wake of its own in the `dsn_ask` signal, and it does not suppress that signal (declared keys are classified before the routing opt-out). This key is read by the web-chat shell rather than by the pane, and it is stripped before the service's trust fingerprint, so it never re-asks for approval. When you mount this component yourself, note the asymmetry: `routing` goes INSIDE `params`, while `signals:[{key:'dsn_ask', wake:'queue'}]` goes at the TOP LEVEL of the use_component call.
